accepted_review_findings:
[reviewer finding R1, minor] The converse says: if some k != k' has [C]_{k,k} < [C]_{k,k'} + 1/((q/p)^{t-1} - 1), then model t-1 fails on the noisy class-k instances labelled k' 'and thus fails to achieve 100% population accuracy'. The proof (App. K.1) derives this from the noisy-instance condition (60), which applies only to instances that exist, i.e. it needs [C]_{k,k'} > 0. Counterexample under the package's own framing (conditions at given n and lambda, WC-F29): take noise-free labels, C = I, and t = 2. Then (11) for any k' != k reads 1 < p/(q - p), which holds whenever q/p < 2. That is attainable, e.g. with K^2 n lambda large and n(c - d) < 1 - c, or with K^2 n lambda held at a constant below 1 - c as n grows. But with C = I the clean-instance entries (WC-F20) give the teacher a margin q > 0 at the true label, so model 1 classifies every instance correctly. The 'thus fails to achieve 100%' conclusion is therefore false. The same holds for every pair k' outside the superclass of k, where the premise forces [C]_{k,k'} = 0. WC-F17 restates the claim without this caveat; WC-F27 and W7 make the converse the only allowed route for asserting failure; and W2 ('must not change ... premises') plus rubric J2 ('converse < with exponent t-1') could penalise a writer who correctly adds the qualifier [C]_{k,k'} > 0. The fact faithfully reports the source, but the package presents a false statement as an essential theorem component with no caveat, unlike the comparable source flaws it does caveat.
Required repair: Add a maintainer caveat (kind 'unknown'/open_caveat, or append to WC-F17 as a labelled MAINTAINER NOTE). It should say that the converse's failure conclusion requires that class-k instances with given label k' exist ([C]_{k,k'} > 0, hence h(k) = h(k')), as the App. K.1 derivation from (60) uses. Without that, the converse can fail, e.g. for C = I when q/p < 2. Verify this against App. K.1 (p. 35). Then update task.md W2/W3/W7 (and rubric J2/J7) so that stating the converse with this qualifier, flagged as a writer derivation or citing the new caveat, is explicitly allowed and not penalised as a premise change. Optionally add it to the W8 caveat list. Recompute the facts.json/task.md/rubric hashes. Do not change any other scientific fact.
